text: If you are highly motivated by beer - you're gonna have a good time here. Wide selection of beer, from the foreign to the freshest of fresh, and even a lovely Irish Cider you really don't see out and about much. I want to set aside the beer component of MKT for a moment and just talk about the food. I have long had a mixed opinion of the Century groups enterprises. While always a fan of Delux Burger Bar, trips to the Century Room have been hit and miss, and 100 just always struck me as incredibly weird. I was there once in a suit and felt massively under dressed. (No, it was not my birthday suit.) So it was with some trepidation a friend and I visited MKT a week ago Wednesday for lunch, to see what it was all about. Hot off a decent Edmonton Journal review, I was optimistic. I got very worried when the waitress informed me that the soft pretzels were off the menu, since they had not come in yet as the truck was running late. Little red alarm bells fired in my head: soft pretzels are so easy to make, I'm really only expecting frozen premade pretzels from Rexall Place and Commonwealth Stadium, or a chain event like Elephant and Castle. My meditation on "what does this *mean* about the kitchen?" was interrupted by the waitress informing me that while the computer button was still disabled, the kitchen indeed was prepared to serve pretzels. The brief rejoicing was interrupted by the pretzels. Bland, dry, tough, no sign of seasoning on the crust. Sure, the sauce accompaniments were tasty but cheese sauce and two mustards are hard to really give credit for. I expected my pulled pork sliders to be a safe bet, seeing as it draws from the Delux stable of tasty burgers-n-things. Unfortunately the bread was very dry, and the filling just tasted of the slaw, with the slightest hint of pork. The side was fresh made chips, but at least a quarter of the order was soggy. My lunch partner had a Thai lettuce wrap appetizer as her main, and while the components were fresh enough they were the definition of unremarkable. The chicken seemed to be just squirted with a Thai sauce after grilling, with a few sauteed julienned veggies mixed in. Don't get me wrong, it was all ...fine. But that's it. Just .... fine. Knock a few bucks off and strip the place of pretension and I might even eat there again. By far the most disappointing part of the meal was the visit from the manager. When I started to answer her question about how the food was, she immediately directed me to fill out a comment card as they were "taken very seriously". I would have preferred to complete the conversation she initiated, thanks. I will drink here any time (hey, wanna get a beer?), but I'm only going to be eating here when circumstances dictate, it's just not a place I'd choose.

text: Ellenberger is a great little park and just what this neighborhood needs. There is a playground for the kids, a swimming pool, football field, a baseball diamond, tennis courts, and a building that was an ice rink. There is plenty of shaded space with mature trees, and a creek that runs through the south side of the park. I used to come sledding here on the hill when I was a little girl, and now I use the hill for lunges and running up and down for exercise. There are a couple small trails (very small) that can be used for running or walking. Many people walk their dogs through the park. There's a shelter on the east side of the park. Our derby team used it once for a picnic. We use the old ice rink to practice in. I'm not sure if it's still going on, but at one point, there was futsal (sort of like indoor soccer) in the same space. You might find a symphony in the park or the farmers market when the weather is nice. Really, this park is a staple in keepting the east side community developed and healthy and helps to make Irvington what it is right now.

text: The town of Phoenixville, PA definitely is like a phoenix rising from the ashes. The towns' main street (Bridge St.) is wonderful. Daddy Mims is nicely decorated, clean, and friendly. Cajun/Creole food is inspired by the French cuisine. We both ordered the Tour of New Orleans and unsweetened iced tea. When a restaurant charges $100+ for dinner (2 people) you should expect perfection. Daddy Mims got the French Bistro part of SUPER SMALL portion sizes to a tee. First Course: Creole Seafood Gumbo - The soup was flavorful but barely coated the bottom of the large soup bowl (maybe 4 oz.). The crab meat was all broken up from stirring the pot. Where is the andouille and okra? Second Course: Commander Palace style shrimp remoulade - There were two large shrimp (yes two !!!) on the plate with a nicely spiced remoulade sauce and garnish. Taste was good what there was of it. Shrimp cocktail usually comes with six shrimp. Do you think they could at least serve four shrimp? Third Course: Shrimp etouffee served over jambalaya and Cajun style roast pork shoulder with smoked bacon over mashed sweet potatoes - Once again, two large shrimp on about 1 cup of jambalaya. The jambalaya was flavorful but unremarkable. I make better jambalaya as does Zatarains. Next to the jambalaya was about 1 cup of mashed sweet potatoes with a small amount (maybe 1 oz.) of pulled pork shoulder strings. The sweet potatoes were excellent. Fourth Course: White Chocolate Bread Pudding with whiskey sauce - This desert is to die for. I can not say enough about how GOOD this was. Go to Daddy Mims just for this desert. Skip the rest of the Taste of New Orleans. Yum !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Beverage: Unsweetened Iced Tea - The tea was weak. The tea bag was waved across the water. Sweetening options limited to sugar and Equal. Luzerne Tea is available in this part of the country. Luzerne is a southern robust tea not like a woossie Tetley. The service was very good to excellent. On a Sunday evening there were four two-top tables (besides us) and a party of six table being served. Maybe the crowds are getting the feed bag on somewhere else before coming to get the bread pudding desert later. Rating (max 4 stars): Overall - 2 stars. Value - 0.5 star. Food - 1.5 stars. Service - 3 stars. Atmosphere - 2.5 stars. Finally, I will never pay $40.00 for the Tour of New Orleans again due mainly to the portion sizes. If it were not for the desert this meal would have been a total rip-off. Americans want a good meal, large belly busting portions and low low prices. We are NOT the French !!!!!!!!!!!!

text: I can't believe I haven't re-reviewed Cafe Cioccolato. Time to rectify that! Some people have daily latte fixes; I have weekly decadent chocolate fixes. There are a good number of chocolates that owner David regularly keeps in the case (Those caramels, raspberry-filled and hazelnut varieties are my faves) but he also orders plenty of new things to try. Josh isn't a huge chocolate fan, but even he has his favorites - he likes the cappucino and peanut butter varieties. And chocolate-covered espresso beans? Josh bought a big bag last night! Moreover, the shop now makes special treats! Sometimes they're seasonal and sometimes they're based around which ingredients David has in stock, but he makes homemade chocolate-covered marshmallows (GIANT!), chocolate-covered raspberries (They look like nut-caramel turtle clusters, but they're filled with whole raspberries!), chocolate-covered oreos and chocolate-covered strawberries. As you might imagine, the strawberries are wildly popular, especially around Valentine's Day, so when we stopped in last night, the stock was fresh out. But when they're available, GET THEM. The berries are huge and fresh, and the chocolate is decadent. They - and all the other delights in the cafe - are a special treat for a romantic dessert or work victory.

text: This is the real Tucson. Had I not gone, would have been one of the worst decisions of my life. I have since dragged well over 20 people here who have in turn done the same. I get serious, heroin-style withdrawal from not eating here often enough, so be forewarned! Aqui con el Nene, or "Nene's" as they are often referred to, has THE BEST chicken I have ever had at any mexican restaurant EVER. Did you hear me? Cuz ill say it again if I have to. BEST CHICKEN EVER. So juicy and flavorful, my mouth is watering thinking about it. Carne Asada...fantastic. Sonoran Hot Dogs: most of the people Ive brought here who have also been to guero canelo (widely regarded as best sonoran hot dogs in town) have preferred Nene's take better. I have tried many of their items: burritos (best tortillas in town), caramelos (kinda like quesadillas with meat), Tortas (omfg delicious)...the list goes on and on. Salsa bar is extensive and well stocked. You could practically make a meal out of just that. All meals come with fresh grilled green onions from their mesquite grill in the back. At night, theres a guy who sells homemade empanadas in several dessert flavors that are a good deal and really really delicious. The food is cheap and good with only one exception in my mind. The soft tacos, while delicious, are pretty small and not quite worth the price IMO, considering the burritos are like 10 times the meat and only double the price. Sundays are hot dogs only, which i really wish they didnt do. And not going to lie, there has been once or twice that Ive rolled on over, and the cart was...gone! And my heart broke. Despite all that, I still give this place 5 stars. Read my other reviews, that should tell you something. Go here, for goodness sake. YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT!

text: Inconsistent inconsistent! Each location is like a totally different experience, it is a complete crap shoot between the locations. It felt like I was walking up to a prison cafeteria to get my gruel. On with the review of the food. The sauce on the pizza was consistent with taste. The sauce on my personal traditional crust pizza was lacking severely, it didn't have the same amount of sauce that I get from Wayne. Also the size of the pizza was skimpy, The overall size of the pizza was smaller, and the slices were smaller, I feel like was was robbed a solid two slices, another inconsistency which I noticed was that they placed the pepperonis under the cheese?!? This baffled me, and I almost thought she got my order wrong. After carefully examining my pizza (in my picture) I noticed the pepperoni were there, and I think this was an option to save some pepperoni. Do I really care about this tactic? YES! The best part of pepperoni pizzas in a flame broiled oven is that the edges get a little crispy. The blanket of cheese stops this from happening. I think you are gambling every time you walk into a Cosi, because you are at the mercy of the person preparing or cooking the food. A positive to point out they do not have waiters/waitresses, however they usually have employees walking around to each table to bring you your food and to take away your trash when you are done. Oh yeah, that is another inconsistency with this location, the restaurant was absolutely empty, me and another lonely person listening to Pitbull at nightclub like volume (not exactly relaxing music for dining). With that mentioned, you would think one of the 5 employees would come out from behind the counter to see if you needed anything. Exton and Wayne locations can do this during a super busy lunch hour. This place seemed like they couldn't be bothered. Maybe if everyone just goes to Larry's for their food Cosi will understand the importance of their customers. So let me talk about the good stuff there. They are very consistent in the desserts, they have a great blondie brownie, and their chocolate chip cookies are fantastic (I am starting to wonder if they are shipped in from a corporate warehouse). I haven't experienced the s'more's dessert, however I heard very good things about it. So I think you can depend on the desserts. Also they have breakfast, sorry I haven't tried this either. I believe if Cosi had the consistency with their 1) food and 2) customer service they would have a chain that could rally against Panera Bread. It's a good stop off for a quick bite and is reasonably priced. I'd think that if you were going out with a bunch of friends for beer, this could be a good choice. text: Definitely the place to have sushi in Tampa! I was in town for business and got hungry for sushi. I looked up a few places close to my hotel to check some reviews. I eat at a lot of sushi places around the country and have NEVER seen one that was this full. (good sign) Truth be told, I was about to leave because I hate waiting. Rarely is the wait for the food worth it compared to another place with no waiting. However the host and hostess were very friendly and convinced me to stay with little effort. I sat at the sushi, ordered a large bottle of good cold sake, and asked if the chefs were allowed were to help me with it. (too much for just me to drink) They were allowed, and off we went. I got some recommendations on what to try from the bartender and also the chefs, who both recommended the same thing for my tastes, Jersey Shore Roll. I then got some very fresh Yellow Tail sashimi, and then a quail egg shooter. What a great meal! Everything was very fresh, perfect cuts, and the service was very friendly and helpful. Next time I'm in Tampa, I will be coming back! Thanks guys! Chancy from Texas

text: My boyfriend and I decided to get out of the city for a day and spend some time in Bucks County. Chose to go to this winery mostly out of convenience and were somewhat disappointed. Maybe you'll like this place more if you like sweet wines. We don't. We did, however, buy a bottle of Rose, for the summer. It was nice, but no different than any other rose I've had. What we were really disappointed in was the service. Staff seemed friendly enough, but it took forever to get someone to give us a tasting. Additionally, the staff didn't tell us ANYTHING about the wines as we were trying them. Just poured and walked away. Maybe some of this is because they were pretty busy that day, but then you should put more staff on the tasting bar. I like to learn about the wines, how they were made, where the grapes come from. But we got nothing! $7 for a tasting of 5 wines and you get to keep your glass, so that's fun I guess. Altogether, a very "meh" experience. text: If you are looking for a long distance mover this is not the place to go. I have moved across country multiple times and this is the singularly worst move I have ever experienced. Everyone is very friendly and reassuring but I found that they had limited knowledge about the important details of the move and although they will sympathize if things go wrong, no concrete actions will be taken on your behalf. For cross country moves as mine was (Louisiana to California), they only serve as agents for Atlas moving so when your goods are picked up, they are not immediately placed on the transit vehicle. Instead they are placed in storage at their facility while they wait for a driver. After asking multiple times, it is still unclear how your shipment gets assigned to a particular truck. What is clear is that my shipment was not assigned to a transport vehicle, and all the agents seemed to be able to do about it was tell me week after week that they hoped a driver would materialize. This went on for three weeks which also happened to be the contractual delivery window. By the time my goods reached me it was over four weeks after the pick up date and over a week past the promised delivery date. I had already started work and had to completely re-arrange my schedule and take time off just after starting the job because they were completely inflexible with the delivery date. This, in spite of the fact that they were outside the contracted delivery period. The only option given was an additional charge that would amount to almost 50% of the move cost and they would place my goods in storage (again) and deliver them two weeks later. This would have been six weeks after they picked them up. I had initially been impressed with how nice everyone was but at the end of the day, none of that mattered. I was left with a major problem, they did not fulfill the agreement and they would not make any concessions in spite of having put me in a very difficult situation. Using them was a big mistake, I've had better experiences with United Van lines and independent movers.

text: I was actually really impressed with this hotel. Holiday Inn hotels don't have a great reputation for comfort, they're mostly a cost-conscious choice. I only payed for one night in a king size room (two large beds and a desk), and the uni picked up the tab for the other 2 nights (total of 4 days). I didn't have any children eating or rubbing the carpeting, so I don't need something that achieves that standard of sanitation. I was traveling with an S.O who spent the majority of his time at the room, so the fact that he thought it was tidy and well appointed probably stands for more than my experiences. The first night we got in late and were a little worried that we should have called to let the hotel know. They were incredibly nice and friendly at the desk, even though I was totally exhausted after a 13 hour drive. There was a big basketball game going on nearby, and the hotel parking was being shared for the event, but I was impressed that even with that all going on, we still found a spot quite easily. Nashville has a lot of open sewage vents that can smell pretty funky if you're downwind, but that's not the hotel's fault -- or anyone's fault -- that's just the city. Like Paris, I think its just a little stinky at times. (Actually, a lot of my experience in this city reminded me of Paris: lots of old run-down parts that were quirky at best, punctuated with modernized attempts at genuine luxury and comfort.) The room was big, with a nice balcony and a very new shower/bathroom area that was clean and modern. Even as close to the elevators as we were, the room was almost silent, which was pretty impressive to me. The shower head had a massager setting and was really big, and the tiling looked granite. I am allergic to feathers, so I definitely appreciated that there was synthetic pillows and bedding available without a fuss. The room was also super warm when we got in, which was wonderful, since we live in FL and were horrified by the burning cold and snow. The only real annoyance in the room was the television, which had a un-bypassable menu system before allowing access to the unpaid, normal channels. All it meant was that we left the tv on mute when we would have otherwise shut it off. I always wish there are more power outlets. The towel aviary was awesome. I totally wish I could do that. The hotel restaurant hosts local musicians, and we went there for dinner on our first night. The quesadilla I ordered was absolutely delicious and fresh tasting. The only negative thing I could say was that in the full restaurant of music audience, few people were eating/drinking and I would have liked for those people who were trying to get dinner (like myself) to get a bit more attention than the patrons who weren't ordering anything or were only drinking Bud. The music was nice, and honestly, if I hadn't been so hungry, I probably would have appreciated the intimacy that our server's absence left us. All in all, the location was great (SO close to my interviews!). The room was clean and nice, with an obvious effort toward a modern look. The desk staff were incredibly helpful about things to do and how to get from place to place.
label: POS

text: In case you were wondering, this is a handmade dumpling house. We also had this giant empanada-type dumpling filled with chives, superthin rice noodles, and egg. It was pretty delicious. I think they're usually called "chive boxes" in English, but I forget what they're called at this restaurant. On the not-so-great side, the soup dumplings weren't the best I've had; they tasted fine but the skin was a bit lacking in integrity so they came out semi-collapsed with most of the soup already leaked out. Also, the regular plastic spoons they give out aren't sufficient for soup dumpling consumption. But they're a new restaurant so maybe they'll work out the kinks and improve. It's cash only for now, but the food here is cheap so that's acceptable. I'll definitely be back for the aptly-named "delicious dumplings".

text: Yeah...no. I'm really not sure where all these stars are coming from. My experience was less than spectacular. I think this food truck has glimmers of potential, but it has a very inconsistent image, which if you really think about it, is kinda ironic and funny because they bill themselves as "Floribbean". I've been putting off reviewing Shell's because of this, but tonight, I ran across Catherine W's review, and was like, "Ohmigod, I'm NOT crazy!". Like Catherine, I tried them for the first time at 4Hands Food Truck Fest, and if you read my truck fest review, yes, we didn't get there until the latter half of the festival. Shell's had run out of more than half of their offerings, including their Cuban (which was my first choice), so my choices were limited, which may have played a part in how they turned out, but I'm not convinced that should be an excuse. Prices are pretty reasonable and in the ballpark with other food trucks. You can order a salad for $6.00 or you can go with a sandwich with sweet potato chips or two tacos with two sides for $7.50. They do take credit cards. So after debating my choices since I couldn't get the Cuban, I got into line with three people ahead of me. It took me about ten minutes to get to the head of the line. I ordered fish tacos with flour tortillas, sweet potato chips, and the cactus salad. Once I ordered, it took another 20 minutes to get my food...there were apparently four or five people ahead of me. And yes, I appreciate them cooking it to order, but honestly, I don't know why they do it because by the time I walked back to my table 10 yards away, the fish was lukewarm. Devise a method to cook in batches or something and keep it under a heat lamp or something...because cooking it to order didn't really make much of a difference here. Because not only was the fish taco lukewarm, it was all bland. The description is written as fish, grilled onions, shredded lettuce, diced tomatoes, cilantro, and key lime crema. Really? Okay. So I remember tasting the fish. And the tomatoes and lettuce. But the onions, cilantro, and key lime crema, while physically there, didn't do anything to the tacos. Actually, I'm pretty surprised that it was key lime crema because there was no key lime taste to the sauce at all. At least my tacos did not fall apart. The cactus salad was not what I really expected; I would really have to describe it as sour pickled green beans. Not really my cup of tea. The only redeeming factor in the meal was the sweet potato chips...they are pretty good. So, if you read my fest review, I mention that everyone had run out of bottled water by 6 PM, and that it was a food truck that had casually mentioned it. Well, Shell's was the food truck; while I was standing there waiting for my food, she said it to a customer who was inquiring about water. And all I really want to say is that, you had like three people working, and one of the reasons why I wanted to try you guys out is that one of your employees was taking a break at a nearby table and was talking your truck up like it was the best thing in the world. And if your employee has the time to kick it up and if your menu is half gone anyway, with the little business sense I have, wouldn't it make sense to send an employee out on a water run? We ordered a Roma which had the thinnest possible slices of roma tomatoes you could probably ever cut, PAPER THIN! It looked ok enough but the toppings were skimpy to say the least. On to the taste.. oh how to describe it.. bland, that word comes to mind. We added salt and that parm cheese on the table it was so bland and the crust honestly reminded me of a bad, old Aunt Annie's pretzel that lacked rise time. Seriously those of you who know my reviews know that I don't pull any punches, when something is bad its bad and I stay honest to my experiences. Have you ever heard the saying there is no such thing as a bad pizza? Well that is not true! Pie Pizza and Pastas in Metry has it. With Slice, Reginelli's, Theo's, and Pizza Delicious there is just no good reason to risk it on this place. I honestly felt nauseous after we ate and for several hours after, not a good sign. The waitstaff? attentive... OVERLY attentive, trying to get the best tip possible because there are no other customers attentive, check on you every 5 minutes attentive, ask you how your meal is RIGHT after you took a big bite of food attentive... you get my drift. The menu equates to the odd dark dungeon decor, it all just doesn't add up. So as you may be able to tell, I will not be back. For those of you who gave this joint 4-5 stars (for being open late or getting a coupon), well, please stop doing that! Now I just need to figure out which box I will check for "ambience" on this review..

text: Summary: Great food, big portions, kind of expensive! Remember when all your friends were turning 21 one-by-one? Remember all those crazed nights, with the sheer awesomeness of complete randomness? Yeah. This was one of those nights. (Gosh... now I feel old) Anyways... I'd gone here with 2 of my friends, one of whom was turning the glorious two-one. We had drinks (both variants - some boozed up and some sans-alcohol) flowing all through the night, appetizers, entrees, and dessert. Aka, we didn't skimp out on anything. We went for the real deal. (Disclaimer: For the safety and security of your wallet and credit line, I recommend that you avoid doing this.) Libations consisted of several different margaritas (El Vez, Pink Cadillac, and Golden), some specialties (Julep and Sangria Blanca), and the Michelada. They make great variants of most of them in the virgin and alcoholic variants, and I personally can attest for the awesomeness of the Sangria Blanca and the Michelada. The Sangria was absolutely spot on - correct sweetness, correct flavoring - and it hit the spot. Appetizers were the traditional El Vez guacamole (awesome as usual - get it), the Mexican Chopped Salad, and the Queso Fundido De Hongos. I wasn't particularly fond of the latter two, but as I mentioned, go for the guacamole. You won't be sad. Then again, the Queso was a hit at my table, but just not with me, so take my recommendation with a grain of salt (or cheese?). Mains consisted of the pollo annatto, the huarache de hongos (vegetarian), and the pasilla braised pork. I can't speak for the non-veg dishes, but the huarache was absolutely phenomenal. The sauces were spicy and delectable, the veggies were cooked perfectly, and they were awesome. The other guys really liked their mains too, so I'd venture to guess that all 3 are pretty good. Dessert was just churros and flan. Oh wait. I can't say 'just.' It was AWESOME churros and flan. Really really good stuff. Mouth-gasm inducing stuff. Yeah. That good. Other friends who've visited haven't raved as much about the desserts, so maybe it was just good luck on a good night, but they were fantastic. Service was great as well, and our server was very helpful and attentive to our table, even though the place was packed and she had a ton of other tables to work with. The one downside? 65$ per person (78$ including tip) at the end of the night. Granted, we had a ton of food and drinks, it was a great evening, and going in, we knew that our wallets would be lighter at the end of the evening, but some of the items are still overpriced. However, if money is no concern - go here. It'll be a fun visit. If it is a concern... well. Save up! :)

Going back and forth between the sauces was my favorite part, with the winner being the House. The Ancho Blackberry was probably my least favorite as I tend to prefer savory over sweet, and this sauce was a little too reminiscent of jam. Kudos for creativity, though. I saved the cornbread muffin for last, and this is probably what saved this joint from a 1 star. Little chucks of corn highlight what turned out to be the winner of the dish. I wouldn't tell you not to go, and I may give it another try. It's just that this concept needs some work. Here's what I would do. Get a real space with seats and a door so folks want to stick around. Lose the ciabatta and go with a nice, soft absorbent bread. text: This place is a great place to grab a glass (or bottle) of wine with friends. It's also a romantic spot to take the wife to before dinner. What am I referring to? There is a couch with a couple of chair immediately inside to your right. If that's not your style, there are several seats at the bar. If you're there with a group they have several indoor tables. In the mood for a night on the patio? Well you can choose the front one, which is enclosed from the wrath of mother nature, or sit out back next to the warmth of a fire pit. All are great options! I do feel it is worth noting that when sitting out on the back patio we have had slow service a couple of times, which is honestly the only reason I don't make this 5-stars. We've never been in a hurry though and just gives us more time to enjoy the wine. Best of all, for the dog lovers out there, they do welcome dogs on their back patio! While we always bring our own water dish, just in case, they have always provided us with a water bowl. Plus they usually bring our little guy a treat as well. Ok so realizing most people don't care about bringing fido to a wine bar...I will move along to the important stuff, the wine selection. 3500 Winehaus has a variety of options to select from. They have about 15-20 different wines you can select by the glass, or you can opt to select a bottle. If you do go the bottle route they do have options for just about every price point. Starting out at the $20-range and heading on upwards with their "reserve" listings like Camus at $90. The bottles are broken down into convenient categories such as "bold, spicy reds" or "earthy whites," with a generous description of each wine they offer. One of the things that I feel 3500 Winehaus does a good job of is ensuring they offer wines from a large variety of growing regions. Whether it's France, Italy, California, and even the less heralded regions like New Zealand and South America. So there you have it...a nice, neighborhood wine bar that is practically around the corner from us, that is dog friendly? Yeah, we're sold!

text: Sometimes I relish in being a contrarian, but in this instance, I almost regret my dissatisfaction. August was the one thing I had to do according to Peter D, Brooklyn's Finest in Nola recs. I don't do it intentionally or ostentatiously for the sake of being different and against the grain. In a short summary, the food was average, and the overall experience was brought down by the subpar, I mean, shockingly subpar service considering the class of venue this is purported to be. I arrived at 1pm, excited, wearing a fly ass dress for lunch with my boo. I was greeted by a plain blond in a faux Pucci printed shirt in cheap, so naturally I assumed the guy in a white button down was the actual host. It turns out he was a busboy. No, I wasn't drunk yet. I just don't read clothing signals the same way. We were then greeted by our waiter who presented us with menus and asked if we wanted wine or cocktails to go with our lunch. We did. He returned with an extensive wine list, but no cocktail menu. It wasn't until he came back to speak to us about drinks did we even have a chance to ask for this menu. I started with August's "old-fashion" which included blood orange and vanilla bourbon. I don't know why I thought this was a good interpretation, because in hindsight, vanilla bourbon is a terrible idea. He had the Hemingway, which was rather refreshing, ok, we were off on a decent note. The baguettes seemed a bit under baked, or do we just like bread albino down here? In any case, I began with an heirloom tomatoes salad as appetizer - as the tomato festival was to take place that weekend. It was a little delicious. I say a little, because the salad consisted of 4 cubes of fresh tomatoes, 4 leaves of greens, 2 cubes of watermelon, and 2 cubes of cantaloupe. The cubes were the size of standard dice. I did the prix fixe lunch menu. He had a blue crab, truffles gnocchi, infinitely fancier options from the a la carte menu. Blue crab is the business. I liked this dish a lot, but the gnocchi had no bite at all, it was way too mushy. It was over before my tongue even registered its existence. Uh huh, that's what she said. My main was brandade de morue ravioli? First of all, I always thought that brandade de morue was more of an appetizer, but I guess since it's in ravioli, we can call the 4 pieces of baby ravioli a meal. In any context, it was good if a little bland. His short ribs and mixed veggies salad combo was average. Short ribs just aren't the business. Finally for dessert, I got some peanut butter chocolate crispies with "buttered popcorn" ice cream. Took two bites and left it mostly untouched. At this point, we'd been tended to twice by our waiter and not more by the busboys, by contrast, our neighbors, a group of older ladies pretty much had a personal waiter table side from the start to the finish of their meal. Finally, the waiter came around and asked if we enjoyed dessert, consider the miniscule portions, it wasn't uneatened because we were full, don't you think? I don't think at this point, we should've had to outright say, no, this sucked. No, I think for us to say, no, it wasn't what we were expecting, he should've insisted on getting us a replacement to try to salvage the meal. This isn't some random place where any order is a gamble. I really feel like August took advantage of its fame and acclaim too much.

text: Yea. I loved this place. The beauty was that we went as a party of 6 and all of us love tasting and sharing, so we pretty much ordered everything. Fried Brussles and Bacon : I hate brussles sprouts, but guess what? Seared Scallops : We liked this so much we ordered it 3 times. The Rice Pudding underneath was a surprisingly perfect complement. Oysters : Fresh oysters were available. We tried a couple different kinds and found them to be awesome. Second Course : Catch of the Day : Last night it was Tile Fish and it was prepared really well. Grilled Tuna : Solid, but I didn't get to taste it so I can't comment much on it other than what I heard. Garganelli : This was quite a simple pasta dish but I loved it. The Broccolini was cooked quite well, but unless you're a veg, I would choose something else since it's not a standout. Skirt Steak : Some of the best I've tasted. Very nicely cooked. Well done. Veal Sirloin : I was kind of skimpy on the accolades for the other second courses cause this one was simply one of the best things I've ever had (anywhere). Get this if you can and I hope it's just as good for you. Third (dessert): Chocolate Ganache Cake : One of my top 5 deserts, if not the best (hard to choose) but wow, this thing was amazing! Pound Cake : At this point I was full of food and wine and couldn't swallow another thing. But, I hear it was quite good since we had 3 of them on our table and nothing but crumbs left. Cheeese : Our waiter described them well and we chose 4 or so of them and they were well described and tasty! Overall, this was a wonderful meal. I don't think I've ever been out with a group before and seen every single plate finished totally. Nothing was sent back to the kitchen. I looked around and this was not a localized situation. Everyone in the place was eating everything put in front of them. It was really quite good. Now before you go running out there (and don't take a car, there is nooooo parking anywhere), know this: We only went once. It could have been a lucky night for us and another night may not be as good. But I kind of doubt it.

text: What an amazing neighborhood biking/hiking/watersport/relaxing spot. As activites go, I love to walk here, though the only real spots with trails/sidewalk are on the Wisner section past City Park. If you enjoy kayaking, canoeing, or stand up paddle-boarding then this is definitely your spot. You can even rent a kayak at certain spots on the bayou. There are also a few clubs that meet to enjoy sports like running, volleyball, and bicycling all along the bayou. And then, of course, you can just party on the banks of the water. Bring a grill, drinks and friends and sit under a tree anytime you want--who doesn't love that? Did I mention that there is a festival that basically just celebrates partying on the bayou? It is called Bayou Boogaloo and it is wonderful. In a nutshell, this place is awesome and I'm so glad to live close enough to enjoy it!

text: Sometimes, you just want some comfort in the usual. For one wedding anniversary, we tried a new place that had just changed ownership, chef, menu and decor. But it fell hopelessly short of our expectations, and we decided to get a drink and dessert at Park instead. We just KNEW it would be good. Perhaps it is starting to look dated in there. Perhaps they don't have experimental flavors in the menu. Or it isn't a place for the pretty to see and be scene. But I know I can go in, and have a great meal and not have to worry about making reservations days in advance, changing into "nighttime" clothes, or care if my parents feel too out of place eating next to a table of Music Row scenesters. It's just comfortable. Oh and it's up there with Eastland Cafe's (their sister place) happy hour. All drinks are $5, and they have some great snackies to go with them. I'm looking forward to a posslbe return visit, but there are also lots of other NOLA restaurants that I feel are equal to the overall experience we had at Bayona. 4.5 stars for the food but only 3 stars for the service - at a restaurant of this caliber you really have a right to expect excellence in all areas and unfortunately that just wasn't the case on my initial visit.

text: Stopped in for dinner Saturday evening. The tavern is very attractive inside and out. It has a cozy, sophisticated feel to it. The staff is neatly dressed. Great first impression. That was a probably a mistake - it's not obvious when you walk in or sit down, but this is a pretty loud bar. It is difficult to carry on a private conversation over the table. Music in the background was too loud, did nothing for the atmosphere. I know way more than I want to about the couple that sat down next to us. Help was friendly. Loved the classy dresses the waitresses were wearing. Service was no more than average. The floor staff was hustling, but there weren't very many of them. It seems like there needs to be a couple more people on the floor The tavern advertises small plates, no mention of the small menu - this has a "Bar Rescue" feel to it - very tight, very focused menu, 6 beers (nothing local) and maybe a dozen high end mixed drinks. There is a large and comprehensive wine offering. Old folks alert - if you use reading glasses, bring them if you are planning to read the menu. Lighting is low and the print is tiny. The food ranged from boring to the best: Duck Confit - Tasty. However, who ever wrote the menu is embarrassing themselves by even mentioning the lettuce (one piece) or the pickled celery pieces - I doubt the two of them together would constitute 2 calories. Sirloin burger - maybe the best burger I've ever had. Now, it was a $12 burger, no lettuce, no pickled celery, but it was a hellofa burger. Argulo salad - good, nothing special, but $9? There couldn't have been more than $0.50 of ingredients in this. Bruschetta - looked pretty, tasted boring. I really wanted to like this place, but it was too noisy and it didn't feel like a good value. There are better tapas to be had and better bars to drink at. It's a shame, I really liked the feel when I walked in and I might even go back to try it again. Bottom line - $80 for two.

text: Fantastic pressure cooked fried chicken. Always liked that it was made as I ordered instead of laying around. I've made some very large orders for parties through here. text: Scotty's does a lot to attract different types of visitors in town for conventions, which is very nice. However, the food is bland with little flavor. I had a steak sandwich with macaroni and cheese. Both were very boring with little flavor. Scotty's take on German Chocolate Cake was very good, and I would recommend it. The only reason to come here is for the ambiance during certain conventions, dessert, maybe a few drinks and a easy place to meet up with friends. If you're really into sports and need to see a TV in every direction, Scotty's is also the place for you (I am not one of these people). It seems more like a hang out place than a real restaurant.

Admittedly it is a redecorated Wendy's but I can appreciate that it is being repurposed and is now the location of a new, thriving business. text: Highly Disappointed in this place. Went here for my sister in laws b-day as she used to live nearby, and I think that must be why she has good memories. First of all, the decor is really tacky and unoriginal. The chips and salsa are AWFUL. I mean, you are a Mexican restaurant- you can't even make fresh salsa? It's like 5 ingredients. Instead they give you this liquidy crap, poured straight from a glass syrup jar. It's meant for serving syrup people, NOT salsa. This place is called an American-Mexican restaurant, so I guess that explains some of the weird things on the menu. But when I want Mexican, I want real Mexican...not Mexican-American. I asked the waiter if they made their own taco shells, I should have known better with the chips and salsa...but figured I would ask anyways. He told me that they did, so I ordered the tacos. Tacos come out, and what do i see? Boxed frigging taco shells, how could he say they make them there? Needless to say, I've had better tacos at Taco Bell. My husband didn't care for his burrito either, and he grew up in CA so he knows good Mexican food. I didn't want to ruin the birthday dinner, so I didn't complain...I just knew that I would never be back!

I have no problem with eating in divey places, but how is a po-boy (read: sandwich with no side) and a Pepsi $15 in this kind of establishment? text: When am I going to learn?!?! A friend once told me not to go to a restaurant to try their Restaurant Week menu because often times the food seems mass produced. Makes sense... and it really seemed that way last night. I went to SB with my wife last night for Restaurant Week. We were both really excited because we checked out the menu beforehand. On paper, it seemed so promising. Upon arriving, I really dug the vibe... modern, but not too pretentious... not too noisy with the right amount of background noise. Here's what I got: 1st course... Oyster Po'boy Sliders... really did nothing for me at all. It felt like I was eating mini Big Macs with a leaner meat. It didn't taste bad at all... just had nothing to really make it stand out. 2nd course... Fried Green Tomato salad... again, did nothing for me at all. The salad and side dressing had no flavor at all. Come to think of it... the fried tomato seemed to not really have any flavor at all. 3rd course... Beef Short Rib with creamy polenta, broccolini with roasted mushroom jus... ok, this was awesome. It was hearty, comforting and delicious. The short rib was as it should be, so tender you could cut it with your fork, Good stuff... 4th course... Chocolate Dipped bacon with Caramel corn... this was probably the biggest disappointment of the night. What we got was definitely not what we thought we were going to get. I thought it would be more refined, but it was literally bacon dipped in chocolate over caramel corn. I thought it would at least be chocolate covered bacon crushed up and sprinkled over caramel corn... nope... just my preference though. As for our waiter... I don't even remember his name. I don't even know if he told it to us. A lot of the time, there would be an empty glass on the table and I'd have to flag him down to ask him for something. He was nice, but didn't seem overly attentive. With all of the hundreds of restaurants in the area, I won't be going back to SB. I didn't have anything that made me want to go back. On the plus side, my wife really enjoyed her meal. Me, not so much!!!

Our first course that we ordered did not arrive at the table until 8:45. Granted they gave us free apps to hold us over, but that's not what I came there for. Our 2nd course did not arrive until 9:20 and the 3rd course around 9:50. Dessert came out around 10:15. We did not leave the restaurant until 10:45. I'm pretty sure 3.25 hours is not the experience this establishment was going for and neither were we. Also, we did not finish most of our 3rd course and asked multiple waiters to pack it up for us. Well, to add insult to injury, guess who did not walk out with their leftovers. That's right, they threw them out. The manager extended a 20% discount for the tardiness, but that's not really enough of a discount for such a slow experience. With all that said, I love Moda Mio and Monsu and have never had a problem at either of these places the multiple times I have been to them. Hopefully Popolina will work out the kinks and get it right for future patrons. Otherwise, I can't imagine people will return.

text: I'm a little embarrassed to admit that I never really got the chance to sit down & actually try Miss Saigon's food before I left. I've probably gotten their bubble tea about forty times, but no food. I wanted to try them, since I had heard so many good things & read so many positive reviews about them, but it just never happened. Which sucks, because I've only ever had Vietnamese maybe three times ever. Anyway, I shall review what I have had, which is the bubble tea! I'm a bit of a bubble tea fanatic, & when I moved to Tucson, I was a little nervous that I wouldn't be able to find a place that made it. Thankfully, I stumbled upon Miss Saigon! :) All of the flavors I tried were phenomenal, but my favorite by a long shot is the Honeydew (melon) Snow, with extra boba. Aside from one visit where the tea was watered down (maybe the ice just melted way faster than it should've?) & one visit where the boba joined to form a bumpy, mushy mass of goo, their bubble tea has been pretty reliable. The only real negative I can think of is the price, which I find a bit high at this location. My bubble teas were close to five bucks a pop. At the downtown Miss Saigon, they were just under three if I didn't opt for the extra boba. That's much closer to what I am used to paying in Chinatown. Regardless, I obviously didn't find the higher price point to be a problem. I still bought them, week after week, just because they're that damn good. If you're a fan of bubble tea, I don't need to tell you to go here. If you've never had it, you should definitely swing by & try one! Just go to the location on Campbell, it's cheaper there & they taste the same at both locations. :)
label: POS

text: I wish there was a way to rate negatively. To even give this property one star is a compliment that is undeserved. The property in New Orleans is beautiful. The front desk staff and valet workers upon arrival are very nice. The valet workers even recognized me and spoke to me through out my stay. Unfortunately, the news is not very good after that. I stayed in this hotel for 11 nights because my group of 19 was utilizing the meeting rooms. The first night that I stayed the bathtub had hair in the tub from another guest. I pulled the sheets back on one of the two beds in my room and there was a crusty pizza stain on the sheets. I left the sheets pulled back and slept in the other bed. The next day before lunch I went up to the room and the first thing I noticed was that the towels had been replaced, but a price tag that I had thrown away in the bedroom was on the floor in my bathroom, along with my hair that had fallen out while blow drying it earlier that morning. I pulled the sheets back on the "pizza" bed and the bed had been remade with the dirty sheets! Sheets that were dirty from another guest. I immediately called and requested to speak with a manager. I was transferred to a manager's voice mail. I left a message describing my disappointment and requested that my room be properly serviced. Upon my return to my room that evening at almost 8 p.m., my room was still not cleaned. I called again, was once again transferred to voice mail, so I hung up and called Guest Services again who took a message. I left to eat dinner. I forgot something in the room, returned about 40 minutes ago when I met the evening manager who apologized and said everything would be taken care of. Later that night I had candies delivered by the hotel. The next day my room was not even cleaned! Upon my return at almost 9 p.m. I had to call for fresh towels, which were delivered about 30 minutes later. In the meantime, I had two co-workers that had packages shipped via USPS to the hotel. Instead of the hotel either delivering to the room, or holding at the front desk, they delivered to FedEx, who then charged $18 and $10 respectively for "handling" fees. RIDICULOUS! These FedEx employees were very rude when questioned about these fees. In fact, one of my co-workers said his package would just be destroyed because the cost to return to sender would be too expensive. On the eighth day, the house keeping people exchanged the towels but did nothing else, to include did not vacuum, sweep, clean the tub, bring new shampoo, take out the trash, or even MAKE THE BED! After the first day that I had to request the sheets to be changed, my sheets were never changed during my entire stay. My refrigerator had to be changed out twice which ruined a meat tray that I had purchased for snacks for my group. I ordered room service once and ate in Vitascope a couple of times. The burgers and fries and fried crawfish were excellent, but on the ninth night, I had a steak salad at Vitascope that I purchased to go to eat in my room. I had requested it medium well. The steak was bloody, in fact it had bled all over the lettuce, but it tasted horrible like the steak was spoiled. I couldn't eat the salad at all. (I normally eat my steaks medium rare, but not on my salad.) Other co-workers that were staying there also complained of similar issues: Their sheets had never been changed, one requested his laundry to be picked up, a service that is offered, but wasn't picked up for two days. He complained twice before it was picked up. One co-worker had clothes that were left in his room from a previous guest that were never removed. The meeting room charges for items such as surge protectors, projector screens, etc were outrageous. $20 a day just for a key for the meeting room that was rented! The rooms were straighted every night, but we had to request for them to be vacuumed, I would think this would be automatic. The last two days water nor candies were placed in our room. Out of the 11 days, we were finally given a TRASH CAN ON THE NINTH DAY! Many, many times we would return to our meeting room after the staff had cleaned it to find the meeting room left unlocked with our personal projector and property left unsecured. We would have to call to have security lock the doors. I travel many days a year and am a Gold member with Hilton. I have never had a stay like this in one of their properties. I have to say that I am very disappointed and will absolutely never stay at this property again, not 100% sure that I will choose a Hyatt again. In addition to the candy tray, I was given a $20 comp to Vitascope and milk and cookies at 10:20 p.m. one evening. I was excited to share this city and my home state with my co-workers, but unfortunately they will always relate Louisiana to this horrible hotel stay!

text: My husband & I came here on his last night in town before shipping to boot camp. We wanted something Italian and I require gluten free. Amerigo fit the bill. They had gluten free pasta as well as a variety of other dishes, salads and appetizers available to those of us who cannot tolerate the evil that is gluten. We started with a GF Ceaser salad and found it to be delicious, though a little heavy-handed with the parmesean. Hubby ordered the shrimp bisque and I sneaked a bite (NOT GF)- delicious with a sprinkle of freshly ground pepper. Hubs got the Rosemary Gorgonzola Filet with potatoes and asparagus and it was AMAZING. Everything on his plate was good, I found myself eating more of his dish than I did of mine. I got the GF chicken Picatta with pasta- comes with sauce, mushies, capers and lump crab. It was good but I just couldn't get enough of hubby's dish! The foccacia bread was served warm with olive oil for dipping and I can report that also is yummy. Would definitely go back if I had the opportunity. The price was reasonable, we paid $60 before tip for two entrees, shared salad and a bowl of soup. Service was great- everything was on time, served hot, and pleasant interactions with all servers.

text: Ok, any of my friends know I love this place. Let's get one thing out of the way - it's not the cheapest place to eat in town, generally when the wife and I go here and eat, by the time we're done (cocktails, share appetizer, 2 entrees, bottle of wine, desert) we are in the $150-$200 range. But let me tell you - it's *so* worth it. Plus, you can totally eat there for a lot less than that and you can even order food at the bar if you're in a pinch. We started going to LuLou's probably 6-7 years ago (or more?) and I fell in love with this place from day one. At that time I didn't know a place like this existed in Reno. At that time both the husband and wife team that own the restaurant were there with Colleen working the front of the house and Troy running the kitchen. They were doing amazing dishes and had fantastic service. Then a few years ago Troy got hired as the Executive Chef at the Eldorado and there was a period where it wasn't the same 'LuLou's' experience and the food wasn't quite as good. That said however, for the past 2 years or so they are back on their game and frankly, better than ever. The food coming out of the kitchen is top notch, if you go while Farmers Markets are happening you'll find plenty of ingredients from that including the heirloom tomatoes which are awesome. I think we've yet to find a dish we didn't like at LuLous - their salads are great, especially the 'hearts of romaine' and butterleaf lettuce. One of my favorite entrees is their Ribeye that is served with swiss chard and skinny fries. The steak (I enjoy medium rare) is perfectly cooked and has SO much flavor. The swiss chard, which is a side comes in a little cast iron pot and tastes amazing (enough so that I wish they'd serve it as a separate dish). The skinny fries are amazing and usually anyone else at the table is always grabbing them off my plate - they taste so good! I've tried a lot of their other entrees which are all excellent but that ribeye has to be my favorite. Another MAJOR part of my LuLou's experience is the service. It's top notch. The servers are always friendly and attentive and it's nice to see the same faces when you come back to the restaurant. I'll specifically call out Steve that works there as the man - always goes the extra mile to make sure you have a good experience there (you can request a table in his section if you call ahead/reservations). Personally, I feel that this is one of the, if not the, best places to eat in Reno if you're looking for a fine dining experience. Don't bother bringing your own wine as the corkage is high but the prices are reasonable and the selection is great (some stuff I haven't been able to find locally). Also, please go with the expectation that it's not cheap and that you're going to pay a fair amount for a good meal. Most of the time when I talk to someone that doesn't like LuLou's it always gets back to the fact that they didn't want to spend that much. To enjoy this restaurant - If it's not in your budget, don't go. Lastly, if you're going for a special reason (birthday, etc.) then let them know when you make a reservation and they will go the extra mile.

text: This review is going to be mostly about the service. My wife and I have been regular customers at El Rodeo for at least 5 years now. A couple of the waiters go out of their way to make you feel welcome and are very attentive. This review, however, was not one of those times. This evening (7/19/12) my wife and I ate there. She had a steak and cheese burrito that was mostly burrito and lacking in both the steak and cheese departments, and I have the fajitas rodeo (which consists of steak, chicken, pulled pork, and chorizo) of which the pork and chorizo were pretty good, and the steak and chicken very bland and dry. Halfway done with my meal, I ran out of tortillas and asked for some more. 15 minutes later I went up to the front to request the manager when my server miraculously reappears. I asked him for the manager since the girl at the register was busy and he told me to talk to her. Ok, I said. I then explained to her that I'd requested additional tortillas to finish my meal with, now, 20 minutes ago and never received them, nor had I even seen our waiter until just then. I explained that half my meal was now stone cold, and I wasn't going to be finishing it, with or without tortillas. Instead of trying to make it right in any way, I was informed that the fajitas come with three tortillas, and additional would cost extra. I explained to her that would have been fine, but I didn't feel I should pay full price for half a meal. I then asked if she was the manager, and she informed me that she was not. Undeterred in my quest for a person in charge, someone who would make at least some attempt at salvaging my evening (and my temper) I asked if she could call him and was told flatly "No". "Ok", say I, "when will he be in?". She looks at me with those same darting eyes and says "I don't know" At this point I'd had more than enough, and told her I thought she was lying to me, and the look on her face just confirmed it. Throughout this encounter she and the waiter kept repeating that the entree came with only 3 tortillas, and that it was my fault for not finishing my meal. I gave up, and paid the bill, which I'll be disputing with the bank shortly after wrapping up this review The short, tl;dr version: I had a complaint, and they did not seem to care, nor was there anyone with any authority to make anything right. Moral of the story: This place is mediocre to ok depending on the time of day you eat and how much was leftover from the previous dinner service. text: AVOID AVOID AVOID!! Don't bring your car here unless you want it totally broken. That night I checked the tires myself, I braved the hoards of evil mosquitoes and jacked up my car, crawled underneath with a flashlight and a coin. I checked every single groove of each of the tires they said were cupped, and low and behold, not a single sign of wear. I checked for feathering, inconsistent wear, etc.. nothing. (I used to work in a tire shop). Chalk one up for the crooks at Honda. Go figure that they had an alignment special on at that time eh?? Less than a week later I'm driving around, and I notice something wrong suddenly as I'm driving: inconsistent power, lag when pressing on the accelerator, and unable to go above 4000RPM. I arrive at my destination, and promptly investigate WTF is wrong with my car. Upon closer investigation, I find that the technician that serviced my vehicle DID NOT CLIP DOWN THE HOUSING FOR THE AIR BOX. There was a 1" gap running all the way around the perimeter of the housing. So, for the days prior, my car had been sucking raw air past the throttle body and into the intake manifold. Just GREAT. THANKS FOR THAT ALBERTA HONDA! Clipped it back down after removing the dead bugs and debris from the side of the air filter that was supposed to be CLEAN, and reset the ECU, but alas the issues still persisted. Car would consistently stall as the RPM of the engine got lower. Huge delays in throttle response, rough idle, inconsistent power. And the constant stress of what else they could have damaged as a result of their stupidity. This was frustrating to say the least. One, as my car was busted due to an incompetent tech, and two, who knows how many years of life have been knocked off my car from drawing raw air, dirt, dust, and insects into the intake. The next morning I headed to part source to grab a can of MAF cleaner, as my last ditch effort before having to bring my car back to Alberta Honda. I cleaned off the sensor, hooked everything back up, and took it for a test drive. Hooray, I don't have to take it back to Alberta Honda to have them charge me hundreds of dollars to troubleshoot! Cleaning the MAF worked like a charm. These issues were a DIRECT result of a negligent Alberta Honda service technician, and nearly cost myself and my passenger our lives from getting T-boned after we stalled. I will NEVER bring my vehicle here. I will do my best to ensure NO ONE brings their vehicle here. I regret having purchased my vehicle here, and my next vehicle will not be from here. Letters have been drafted and will be sent to Honda Canada. I encourage everyone else to do the same. Pathetic service. Oh, PS. Trying to charge me $130 dollars for a cabin air filter change?! How stupid do you think I am? Can be done for $12 in less then 2 minutes with no tools.. Don't even have to pop the hood. You should be ashamed of yourselves.

I wanted to post this sentence next: It's not like there's actually blood and fish guts strewn about but it's reminiscent of a fish that has been gutted and left to rot. But I won't. It's just that personally; Balcony Bar doesn't return me any favors aside from a great balcony and decent pizza. The rest of the bar isn't awful as much as it's just incredibly laid back. It's definitely not somewhere that you will find a hopping party hiding around the corner. If you're rebellious, mysterious, or an older patron, you will likely enjoy the downstairs area. And if you're a hipster, young professional or generally a younger-aged patron, you will likely skim right through the downstairs area and head up to your perching post on the balcony. I'm not sure if it's because the stairs are too steep and scary for the former bunch but it's a little eerie how stark the difference is between the downstairs and upstairs areas of this place. I.e.: dance parties upstairs are likely to be welcomed while dance parties in the middle of downstairs are likely to result in criticizing stares. (Even after you decide to head back inside for one more drink after waiting for a cab for 30 minutes, and you now have six Mickey's to drink because of the $10 minimum, and your group is desperate to find a way to pass the time, and it's only 11pm but your first drink was had at a 2:30 LSU kick off... No matter how positively impressive you think your dance moves are at this moment... the downstairs crowd will still not be grateful for the dance party you are trying to create. Trust me.) So to recap this unusually uninspiring establishment on Magazine Street - it's not going to rock your world like some of the other Nola bars I have spotlighted on this blog. BUT with some bias, I biweekly, with breaks in between, am bunched up beside my besties bringin down brews on the beautiful balcony at Balcony Bar. I can't explain the madness. Perhaps I have an affinity for the letter B. Or by chance it's an awkward obsession with balconies (as I have somehow mentioned them 12 times in this post alone). But it's likely that I keep going back because Balcony Bar easily reiterates my favorite saying: "In the end it's not where you are but who you're with that really matters" - DMB(alcony) "Laissez les bon temps rouler" - Barbara Bush (a loyal LoveOurCityNOLA team member) Insider Tips: (1) Not that you don't carry it with you anyway, but be sure to have your ID on hand as there is a doorman most nights of the week and he is perfectly comfortable with rejecting your entrance. Even those who are small, quick, Mexican and squeaked in through the back door have been recognized three hours later and promptly kicked out. (2)Also we're all lucky it hasn't happened yet, so please follow the trend of not falling down the incredibly steep stairs and dying.

text: Once, I stayed in a murder motel in East Nowhere, Texas. I rang the bell, waited a couple of minutes, the attendant came, and I told him I was looking for a room for the night. Him: Single or double? Me: Single. Him: We don't have any. Me: ...A double. Him: Okay. The room had the depressive rank of desperate traveling salesmen on the downward slope of their careers. The bed comforter was authentic from the 1960s. There were paint chips raining into the shower. There was no iron. Still, a better experience than the Ambassador Hotel in New Orleans, because at least I got a room. After arriving at midnight from driving and waiting in traffic for 18 hours, the front desk guy at the Ambassador Hotel gave us a room that was occupied, then a room that was disassembled, then a room that was occupied, and then a room that was disassembled. When my girlfriend called the front desk and mentioned that this was our fourth room and there was an unmade bed and three mattresses piled up against the wall, he told us that Expedia had cancelled our reservation, despite having our reservation confirmed by the hotel earlier in the day, while we were stuck in the aforementioned traffic for four hours. I called Expedia and they told me they had not cancelled our reservation. I choose to believe Expedia. Because it was 1:00 a.m., we decide to give up and sleep in the made bed, but then I have to go downstairs to get towels, soap, and a plunger, because we had no towels, no soap, and no working toilet. Upon checkout, they charge me for the room, though later I learned that Expedia had already charged me for the room. They refunded my double-pay, but still charged me the Amenities fee, which, I suppose, included the amenity of a plunger so I could fix my own toilet. I am not a man accustomed to luxury, but I would at least like a room that I reserved and confirmed. I'm also a man who forgives mistakes, but, fer Pete's sake, I'm embarrased for you if you make the same mistake four times in a row, but then my embarrassment turns to angry frustration when I can see that you're not really embarrassed or interested at all. The little things like asking how my stay was or making eye-contact are meaningful, and were totally lacking from the Ambassador, maybe because they knew my stay probably sucked. On the plus side, the hotel and the rooms looked really cool. If they had management that could instruct the staff to 1) be polite and friendly and 2) know what rooms are available (I don't know; is that asking a lot?), then it would have been a great trip. text: Where exactly do we begin with this place? First off, someone really needs to fix the listing of this place to "KOBA" which it apparently is called now. Only upon calling the location did we manage to figure out "Young Bin Kwan" is now "KOBA." Not even the recent reviewers mention this misnomer. Seriously, how can you guys let this one slip? And apparently this place was Seoul Garden before that? What kind of management musical chairs is going on here? (Edit - I have submitted a Name Change to "KOBA" for this Yelp listing to further help people figure out the real name of this establishment) So logistics aside, what about the food? Well when you go to real Korean BBQ the main thing I usually go for is the KBBQ STAPLE marinated Short Ribs. For whatever reason, there were NO short ribs to be found. In fact, due to the lack of signage at meat buffet area, it is easy for a non-experienced KBBQer to not know what they are getting. This just seems lazy and I regard that as inconsiderate to new or inexperienced customers. Other than that, I found the other mystery meat to be tasting all the same with their marinade. Nothing special at all. I also felt their Kim-Chee and other Korean side dishes to be soggy and mediocre at very best. As for the service, they seemed nice enough, but never really asked if we were new to the location or this experience and I found myself confused on what was the proper protocol. When we got our food back to the table, our server started to cook it for us. Now I have been to several other KBBQs in the past and this totally threw us for a loop. I thought the whole point was for the customers to cook their own meats or whatever they want. Oh and to the reviewer that says there are authentic coals and what not? That's complete BS, all the grills are OLD gas powered grills that aren't very intuitive to operate at all. As for value, well this is a real sour point here. They charge $25 a head for BBQ, and note that does NOT include any other drinks. Soda/Ice Tea/etc is $3.00. And of course, we didn't know until the bill came. By the way, the soda comes to you in a CAN. For $25, I also expected the short ribs to be there, but they weren't. Again that was highly disappointing to say the least. So for two people, you can pretty much expect a $60 bill for KBBQ (possibly without short ribs) not including any gratuity. So if you add a $10 (17%) tip, you're looking at $35 per person. On the Yelp scale, that is "Spendy," not "Moderate." And remember, no short ribs. This place might have been good under Young Bin Kwan, but under "KOBA" this was a complete and total miss. Please beware of this place if you are tempted to go. I would call ahead to see if they actually serve short ribs if you are intending to go and expect them there. We didn't make sure, and we feel burnt (no pun intended). In conclusion, I felt so let down by this place I had to double check that we were even at the right location. I think the real disappointment was because we traveled a considerate distance to go to a place that was rated at the time on Yelp as 4.5 stars, only to fall flat and short of the expectations set forth from these other reviewers. Please consider this a fair warning to anyone trying out this place under the new "KOBA" management.

text: First of all giving Burger Up 1 star is being generous, ZERO stars is more like it! The hostess was sitting at a table eating when my boyfriend and I arrived, she then sat us at a small table near the back/side door entrance with a view of the service station and kitchen. There were many other tables available to sit at. Our server, Andrea was barely a server at all...more of a dancer really as she hung out behind the bar dancing through most of our meal. She got us waters and myself a glass of wine. We ordered an appetizer but I hadn't looked at the burgers yet. She told us we had to order in 10 minutes. We got to the restaurant about 9:30pm but there were still several tables with people dining. We ordered shortly after. As we were eating our appetizer another server/hostess started spraying glass cleaner on the back door we were less than a foot from. Fumes were flying onto the table on our food and in my wine. Not a very appetizing atmosphere! Then my boyfriend recognized one of kitchen guys who was delivering food to the bar. He stopped by our table and my boyfriend asked if he was making our burgers. He said no but yelled at our server (who was hanging out at the bar) saying our food had been sitting in the window for awhile. The food came out and we never saw Andrea again. No check back. Our burgers were way overcooked and my boyfriend had no water left. Then chairs started going up at all the tables around us (we were not the only table left, nor the last table to come in that night). Kitchen floor mats were being dragged by us out the side door. It was freezing outside. I figured I was going to have to get up and print the check myself. We sat there forever waiting for anyone to come by, clear our plates at least. I decided that maybe if I placed my napkin (which was more of a bar rag) on my plate she might get the hint that we were ready to leave. IT WORKED! She brought us the check, never asked how the food was and still are appetizer and entree plates remained on the table. Overall the food was okay but the service was horrendous and inexcusable!!! This was my second experience at Burger Up and the service was bad both times. I don't understand how this place is on a wait everyday. If I wanted to complain I doubt there was even a manager to talk to. All the servers were at the bar mingling, drinking, whatever... It's obvious none of them take pride or ownership of this restaurant which is sad to see. Working in the industry myself I hardly ever complain let alone write a review but this place SUCKS majorly. Maybe they should close and turn it into hipster bar for shitty servers.
label: NEG

text: Ok.... I am from Los Angeles, CA. I'm not trying to sound condescending, but a lot of the restaurants here fall short compared to the restaurants in Los Angeles. Can you blame me? You can't be from Los Angeles, New York, or Las Vegas and expect the food from Tucson to match up. I miss my brazilian bbq, I miss my 24-hour joints, I miss my legit taco stands, I miss my ethnic foods. My goal in Tucson is to find the best restaurants that pleases me and remind me of home. So I have been really disappointed with the quality of the sushi in Tucson, until I came here. My boyfriend and I drove around and 'round looking for a sushi place and I told him this place had really good reviews. Upon arrival, we see a quaint sushi restaurant and park in the lot next to the establishment. The restaurant was full so we sat at the sushi bar. There was one sushi chef (owner) and server working. It took her 20 minutes to take our drink order, but me and my boyfriend are pretty understanding. We felt bad that she had to take on the whole restaurant by herself and she was about my mom's age so I was even more understanding. My boyfriend and I stayed entertained playing hangman with each other. About an hour passes and we're thinking about just leaving, but the sushi chef sees me look at my phone to check the time and he hands us cucumber salad and apologizes. My boyfriend and I feel guilt and stay haha. The wait was totally worth it! The sashimi and sushi were so cold (like it should be! the only place that serves the fish cold, not warm) and melt-in-your-mouth good. We got the sashimi sampler, amaebi, yellowtail, salmon, tuna, masago, albacore, white tuna toro, and I forgot... but they were so good. The white tuna toro was only $7. I remember having toro at Mr. An's for $14! Total rip! Mr. An can go suck it! The meal came with complimentary miso soup and ice cream for dessert. After our meal, the chef asked where I was from and we were talking about Los Angeles and he taught my boyfriend a couple of Korean phrases so that he can impress my mom when he meets her. He explained to us that he usually doesn't expect so much people and we understood about the long wait. All in all, it was really good and by far our favorite sushi place (my boyfriend and I) :D We are visiting tomorrow as a matter of fact.
label: POS

text: Can't these corporate places find a way to get it right? I look around at all the $ they invest in corporate shtick to make the eating experience "cool", but I don't see many of them delivering quality meals. So it was with Famous Dave's. Second trip here. First time was considerably better, but it's been so many months ago i can't remember the details. This time, we ordered a half slab of baby back ribs and a catfish platter. Shockingly the ribs were tough and there just wasn't much there, I felt like I had to fight to get scraps off the bones. The catfish were ok, but cut into small strips which meant we got more breading and less fish. The sides were decent--especially the jalapeno-laced Mac n' Cheese, but the corn on the cob was way overcooked. Someone I worked with awhile back swore to me that Famous Dave's was the best BBQ anywhere in the Midwest. No thanks. I'll stick to King Ribs, Judge's and GT South's, three local Indy spots that do BBQ right. They may not be fancy places, but I know I'm going to get a great meal for the price.

text: I have wanted to try this restaurant for some time. I went there for lunch on a Friday afternoon. So I didn't have any wait time. The décor and atmosphere is very nice, quaint and sophisticated; a good place for a date or dinner with the girls. Plus, the food was pretty good. Because I love seafood so much I ordered the Roasted Shrimp, Lump Crab & Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms for an appetizer. Let's just say that "low cal" does not mean low taste. For this combination I was surprised that it tasted so bland. For my lunch item I selected a portabella mushroom and goat cheese flat bread. This was absolutely great. My friend ordered the garlic chicken flat bread, which was pretty good as well. As a note, I would like to state that this is not a "kid friendly" restaurant. My friend had her little son with her (under 2), whom was not loud nor did he cry during our stay, however, he did knock over our waters 2 times which required some assistance to clean up the mess. I can understand that this is not the type of restaurant that caters to kids. "I get it." However, if I was the waiter, I would not present such frustrations through evident nonverbal gestures. It was very evident that he was annoyed by my friend's son. My friend is a new mom and very sympathetic to the fact that her son may cause a distraction. Plus, a word to the wise, she is a great tipper if she feels you provided adequate customer service. Overall, I believe this is a nice restaurant with great ambiance. I like the idea that they change their menu several times a year so there is always something new to look forward to. Also, I absolutely, LOVE that fact that they have alternative menu options such as low sodium, lactose intolerant, gluten free, vegetarian and vegan menus for HM "high maintenance" guest such as myself.

text: I just went to Roy's Today for my birthday dinner expecting to do the any prix fixe monday menu or wahtever it is called. Had a surprise. Roy, the Roy Yamaguchi, namesake of the restaurant was in tonight for the Tampa location's 12th anniversary. They had a 5 course menu just for the anniversary which was $85. There was a bit of confusion with some of the guests. Per the email you received, if you are a member of the Roy Ohana club, you had to call in to make a special reservation for the anniversary dinner. Well we were technically not there tonight for the anniversary but decided to go with it despite the sticker shock. Heck, it was my birthday and you only live once. A couple tables over, though, there was a party of 10 and they started to complain. One of the managers came over and stated they would honor the prix fixe but from the bar. All in all, i believe the consensus around the restaurant, everyone was there for the anniversary. So we started off with the Kona Kampachi, the first appetizer. The kona kampachi otherwise known as the almaco jack, is in the same family as the yellowtail and amberjack. This appetizer had radishes, hearts of palm, vanilla vinaigrette. This was raw which I am not a fan of raw sushi but this was pretty good. We then had another appetizer, Oysters 3 ways on a half shell. There was a Dynamite Oyster which reminded me of a Dynamite Roll, spicy but amazingly good. The Brie & Crystal Beurre Blanc, just a cheesy ooziness of awesomeness. Pernod Mignonette, which was pretty much to me a raw oyster....was not a fan hehe. The 2 main entrees were the olive oil poached salmon with a sunflower seed risotto, glazed baby carrots. This was just another salmon to me, it was a lil salty. I wish they would have picked another fish like butterfish or mahi mahi. Salmon anyone can have anywhere any time. The other entree was the Wagyu Short rib, which was freaking amazing. The beef melted in your mouth. The pinot reduction with the roasted mushrooms and chard made it probably the best dish. Too bad Wagyu is pricey. Other wise i'd have it alot more. The dessert was a Pink Lady Apple Tarte Tatin.. like a french apple tart with creme fraiche gelato and candied lemons. This was really to die for. awesome. The service was excellent. Our server was on point and explained everything to us. They decorated our table, gave us complimentary champagne. The managers came by. Really enjoyed it. This is the ambience, service I expect to get from Roy's every time I come. All in all tonight was a night to remember, got a picture with Roy, got the service, the food...
label: POS
